title: Differentiable Exact Learning
claim: Compact models trained on tiny datasets generalize far beyond training lengths, reaching the test cap across many tasks.
layout: 2 horizontal-bar panels, shaded training region at left, endpoint badges at right
description: Two side-by-side lollipop-style plots with a shared log-scale x-axis for input length. The left panel covers four arithmetic tasks (mult10, mult2, add10, add2). Each has a red horizontal line that starts at the edge of a tan shaded region, which marks the training lengths, and runs far to the right. Cream labels give the parameter counts and PTO counts, and red badges at the endpoints read ≥1,000 or ≥5,000. The right panel covers ten universal-simulation tasks. Five green lines are unseen tasks and five blue lines are seen tasks. A tan box marks the training range and carries '4,335 Parameters / 75 PTOs / universal'. All lines end in green or blue '≥ 500' badges. The eye goes first to the long lines that extend far past the shaded training region.
caption: Extreme Length Generalization from Small PTO Datasets and Compact Controllers. Length generalization by DFST models trained from scratch on arithmetic and universal-simulation tasks. Shading marks the length of inputs seen during training. Our models see computation traces of inputs with $\leq 3$ digits for addition and $\leq 5$ digits for multiplication. On the universal task, DFSTs see simulation traces of 5 Turing machines on inputs of up-to 5 symbols and generalize to 5 unseen Turing machines. Endpoints mark successful length-generalization reaching a pre-defined testing cap.
abstract: We introduce a framework for differentiable exact learning that couples an unbounded external environment to a state-tracking neural controller, which we train on policy-trajectory observations (PTOs): expert behavior traces that expose observations and actions while hiding internal states. In addition to the learning framework, we introduce Differentiable Finite-State Transducers (DFSTs) which use multilinear updates, support log-parallel training, and emulate arbitrary finite-state controllers, yielding computational universality through environmental interaction. From tiny training datasets, compact DFSTs achieve extreme length generalization on arithmetic and universal-simulation tasks. We replicate the success of DFSTs on RNNs and GRUs, thereby supporting a broader learning recipe: State-Tracking Controller + Unbounded External Environment + PTOs = Extreme Length Generalization. Beyond length generalization, our metric-extraction protocol recovers interpretable discrete controllers from trained DFSTs, which we prove equivalent to the target arithmetic and universal-simulation algorithms. Furthermore, for our Softmax DFST models, simply taking $\mathrm{argmax}$ over the transition probabilities yields discrete controllers which provably exactly perform universal Turing-machine simulation and binary arithmetic. Proving exact learning for the neural controllers requires assumptions, which we empirically support. We make our code, training recipes, model weights, and proof checkers publicly available at https://github.com/fanagor/DEL.
